key_insight: A SCAPS-1D + machine-learning workflow can rapidly rank multilayer perovskite solar-cell stacks and pinpoint the most impactful layer properties for high-efficiency design.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical screening route for optimizing ETL, absorber, and HTL combinations before costly fabrication, including lead-free double perovskite architectures.
method: Simulated 125 ETL/absorber/HTL device architectures with SCAPS-1D.
Trained an ML model on a representative subset to predict PCE for unexplored stacks.
Used SHAP analysis to identify the most influential descriptors and verify top candidates with full device simulations.
evidence_signal: Leave-One-Group-Out validation showed reliable ranking ability, and the top predicted devices were confirmed by SCAPS-1D, including FTO/TiO2/Cs2AgBiBr6/NiO/Ag at 28.85% PCE and FTO/SnO2/Cs2AgInBr6/NiO/Ag at 28.62%.
watch_item: Predictions depend on the quality and representativeness of the simulated training set, so transfer to real fabricated devices may be limited by unmodeled defects and interface effects.
paper_title: Multilayer Screening of Double and Conventional Perovskite Solar Cells Using SCAPS-1D and Machine Learning: Optimization of ETL, HTL, and Absorber for High-Efficiency Architectures
